samples: This module loads a service configuration from a JSON file, validating that the port, worker count, and log level have acceptable values. It reports whether loading failed because the file was unreadable or because the JSON did not match the expected configuration shape. It also provides a default configuration and a fallback-loading helper; the older load-or-default helper is deprecated.

This module loads a service configuration from a JSON file, validating that the port is 1–65535, the worker count is 1–64, and the log level is Quiet, Normal, or Verbose. It reports whether loading failed because the file was unreadable or because the JSON did not match the expected configuration shape. It also provides a default configuration and fallback-loading helpers, though the older default fallback function is deprecated in favor of the customizable fallback version.

This module loads a service configuration from a JSON file and validates that it has a valid TCP port, 1–64 workers, and a log level of Quiet, Normal, or Verbose. If loading or parsing fails, callers can either receive a specific error, use the built-in default configuration, or provide their own fallback configuration. Use `load_with_fallback` rather than the deprecated default-only fallback helper.

This module loads a service configuration from a JSON file, validating that the port is between 1 and 65535, the worker count is between 1 and 64, and the log level is one of quiet, normal, or verbose. It reports whether loading failed because the file was unreadable or because the JSON did not match the expected configuration shape. It also provides a built-in default configuration and fallback-loading helpers, though the older default fallback function is deprecated in favor of the configurable fallback version.

This module loads a service configuration from a JSON file, validating that the port is 1–65535, the worker count is 1–64, and the log level is one of quiet, normal, or verbose. It reports unreadable files and invalid JSON/config shapes distinctly, and also provides a default configuration using port 8080, 4 workers, and normal logging. Use `load_with_fallback` if you want to supply your own fallback; the older default-fallback loader is deprecated.
